extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for claiming the benefit/right of priority to earlier-filed foreign (and international) patent or design applications in U.S. nonprovisional and international applications. Covers timing, form, content, recognized-country rules, restoration, certified copies, and related exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition application statement for post‑March 16, 2013 effective filing dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonprovisional application claims priority to a foreign application filed prior to March 16, 2013 and also contains (or at any time contained) a claim to a claimed invention that has an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013, the applicant must provide a statement to that effect within a specified time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must be provided within the later of: (a) four months from the actual filing date of the nonprovisional application; (b) four months from date of entry into the national stage (per §1.491) for an international application; (c) sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application; or (d) the date a first claim with an effective filing date on/after March 16, 2013 is presented in the nonprovisional application. An applicant need not provide the statement if the individuals designated in §1.56(c) reasonably believe, based on information already known, that the nonprovisional application does not and did not at any time contain such a claim. Nonprovisional international design applications are excluded from the transition provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's certificate priority-claim affidavit/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: When claiming priority to an application for an inventor's certificate (in countries granting both inventor's certificates and patents) under 35 U.S.C. 119(d), the applicant must include an affidavit or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit/declaration must specifically state that, upon investigation, the declarant is satisfied that, to the best of their knowledge, the applicant had the option when filing the inventor's certificate application to file either a patent application or an inventor's certificate application as to the subject matter of the identified claim(s) forming the basis for the priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim in international design applications (Hague) and certified copy timing
rubrics_metrics.description: In international design applications designating the United States, the priority claim may be made under the Hague Agreement and Regulations. In a nonprovisional international design application (not using Hague procedures), the priority claim must be presented in an application data sheet and the certified copy must be furnished per paragraph (g) time periods and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the priority claim was made in accordance with the Hague Agreement/Regulations, present the claim in the application data sheet (see 37 CFR 1.55(m)). Certified copy and other requirements follow the time limits and conditions of 37 CFR 1.55(g). The right of priority under 35 U.S.C. 386(a)/(b) for international design applications applies only to applications filed on or after May 13, 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and timing requirement for priority claims for applications filed on/after September 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after September 16, 2012, the claim for foreign priority must be presented in an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.55(d)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing the required identifying information in the application data sheet constitutes the priority claim as required by 35 U.S.C. 119(b) and 37 CFR 1.55. For international applications entering the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, follow PCT time limits (37 CFR 1.55(d)(2)). For international design applications designating the U.S., see 37 CFR 1.55(m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim acceptable forms for applications filed before September 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed prior to September 16, 2012, the priority claim need not be in any special form and may be made by a person authorized to sign correspondence under 37 CFR 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No special language is required; any expression reasonably interpreted as claiming the benefit of the foreign application is accepted. For such pre-2012 applications the priority claim must appear in the oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 or in an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.55(n)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements for the foreign application
rubrics_metrics.description: A priority claim must identify the foreign application for which priority is claimed by specifying the application number, country (or intellectual property authority), and the day, month, and year of its filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is required for original applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a). For international applications entering the national stage or for international design applications, follow the specific MPEP/PCT/Hague instructions referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized-country requirement for claiming priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The foreign application must have been filed in a foreign country that affords similar privileges to U.S. applicants or nationals, typically a country recognized via PCT, Paris Convention, or WTO membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the MPEP list of recognized countries and WIPO/WTO resources for current status. If a claimed foreign filing was in a country not on the list, an examiner should contact the Office of Policy and International Affairs to determine any status changes. The right of priority is based on the country of foreign filing, not applicant citizenship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same inventor / at least one common joint inventor requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a), the foreign application must have been filed by the same applicant as the U.S. applicant, or by applicant's legal representatives or assigns; interpreted to mean the U.S. and foreign applications must name the same inventor or have at least one joint inventor in common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application where inventorship does not overlap (e.g., sole inventor A abroad and sole inventor B in the U.S.) cannot claim priority even if owned by the same party. Joint inventors may each properly claim benefit to their respective foreign-filed applications. See MPEP §§ 602.xx for correction of inventorship and relevant CFR sections (1.45, 1.48, 1.78).

rubrics_metrics.name: Same-invention requirement for priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: The foreign application must be for the same invention as the U.S. application to serve as the basis for a priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a later foreign application discloses additional subject matter, a U.S. claim specifically limited to that additional disclosure may be entitled to the date of the later foreign application for that subject matter. See relevant MPEP sections for examples and treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelve‑month (six‑month for designs) filing deadline and computation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. nonprovisional application must be filed no later than twelve months (six months for design applications) after the foreign filing date (subject to restoration where available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first day is not counted in computing the period. If the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the action may be taken on the next succeeding business day under 35 U.S.C. 21(b) and 37 CFR 1.7(a). The periods are also subject to PCT Rule 80.5 and Hague Agreement Rule 4(4). Examples and case citations are provided in the guidance (e.g., Paris Convention Article 4C(2),(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing during PTO unscheduled closings and acceptable filing/deposit methods
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO is officially closed for the entire day (e.g., weather), that day is treated as a federal holiday for filing deadlines and the action may be taken on the next business day (37 CFR 1.9(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the Office is not open for filing, correspondence deposited as Priority Mail Express® with the USPS in accordance with 37 CFR 1.10 or filed via the USPTO electronic filing system (EFS) will be considered filed on the date of deposit. When the Office is open for any portion of the business day, papers are due that day even if an unscheduled event closes the Office for part of the day. Contact numbers and procedures for verifying official closings are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of right of priority (unintentional delay) under 37 CFR 1.55(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a subsequent application is filed after expiration of the twelve‑month (or six‑month for designs) period but within two months of the expiration, the right of priority may be restored by petition if the delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration may be available under PCT Rule 26bis.3 for international applications or upon petition under 37 CFR 1.55(c). A petition under 37 CFR 1.55(c) requires: (A) the priority claim in an application data sheet identifying the foreign application (unless previously submitted); (B) the petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(m); and (C) a statement that the delay was unintentional. The Director may require additional information. If the subsequent application is not a nonprovisional, the petition may be filed in the earliest nonprovisional application claiming benefit to the subsequent application. If granted, no further petition is required in downstream applications; file a copy of the decision to ensure recognition. Note: pre‑AIA statutory bars measured from the U.S. filing date may still apply even if priority is restored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy and translation filing requirement during pendency (37 CFR 1.55(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim for priority and the certified copy of the foreign application (and translation if required) must be filed within the pendency of the U.S. application, unless filed with an appropriate petition (e.g., under paragraphs (e) or (f)) or a petition with fee and showing of good and sufficient cause for delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claim for priority or the certified copy is filed after the issue fee is paid, the patent will not include the priority claim unless corrected by a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323. See MPEP §§ 215.02 et seq. for specifics for applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and §215.03 for prior filings. Priority claims and certified copies must in any event be filed during pendency and before grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT/national-stage timing and procedures for priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications entering the U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 from an international (PCT) application, the priority claim and the certified copy of the foreign application must be filed within the time limits set forth in the PCT Articles and Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PCT deadlines for national-stage entry; in the U.S. it is permissible but not required to present the claim in an application data sheet when entering national stage. See 37 CFR 1.55(d)(2) and related MPEP sections for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference and inadvertent omission protections (37 CFR 1.57(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 21, 2004, a priority claim present on the filing date is considered to incorporate by reference the prior-filed foreign priority application as to inadvertently omitted material, subject to 37 CFR 1.57(b) conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a safeguard when portions of the specification/drawings were inadvertently omitted from the U.S. application, or to permit correction of translation errors when the foreign priority application is in a non‑English language. Applicants are encouraged to provide an explicit incorporation-by-reference statement to the prior foreign application if they do not wish to rely on inadvertent-omission procedures. See MPEP §§ 201.06(c), 217, and §601.01(a) subsection III for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability date for priority under 35 U.S.C. 386(a)/(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of priority under 35 U.S.C. 386(a) or (b) with respect to an international design application is applicable only to nonprovisional applications, international applications, and international design applications filed on or after May 13, 2015, and patents issuing thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This date-limited applicability is reiterated throughout the guidance for international design priority claims; see 37 CFR 1.55(o) and MPEP §213 et seq. and §1504.10 for related details.
